title: HttpClient
summary: Call a server from a service with HttpClient and turn the result into a signal.

quiz.q: Which function in the app configuration sets up and configures `HttpClient` (it is required before Angular 21 and still used for options such as interceptors)?
quiz.explain: Put `provideHttpClient()` in the `providers` of `app.config.ts`. Before Angular 21 this was required for `inject(HttpClient)`; since 21 the client is available by default and this function is for configuring it.

quiz.q: Complete the call that asks the server for a list of students.
quiz.explain: `get<T>(url)` sends an HTTP GET request. The type in angle brackets describes the data you expect back.

quiz.q: `http.get(...)` returns an Observable. When does the request actually go out?
options: When something subscribes to the Observable, for example `subscribe()`, `toSignal()` or the async pipe
Only when the app is built
Never; it is only a description
quiz.explain: Observables are lazy. Nothing is sent until there is a subscriber. If you never subscribe, no request is made.

quiz.q: Which method sends a new student to the server?
quiz.explain: POST creates data on the server. The second argument is the body, for example `http.post<Student>('/api/students', student)`.

exercise.task:
Finish `students-api.ts`.

- Import `HttpClient` and `provideHttpClient` from `@angular/common/http`.
- In `StudentApi`, get the client with `inject(HttpClient)`.
- `getAll()` returns `this.http.get<Student[]>('/api/students')`.
- `add(student: Student)` returns `this.http.post<Student>('/api/students', student)`.
- In `appConfig`, add `provideHttpClient()` to `providers`.
- In the component set `students = toSignal(this.api.getAll(), { initialValue: [] })`.
hints: The service needs the client, then two methods that return the request. Do not subscribe inside the service.
`get<Student[]>(url)` and `post<Student>(url, body)`. In the config the providers list is an array.

checks.name: HttpClient and provideHttpClient are imported from @angular/common/http
getAll() sends a GET request for Student[]
add() sends a POST request with the student
The component turns the request into a signal with toSignal
